newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines sees 1996 BOP surplus at $4.0 bln.
newsitem.headline: Philippines sees 1996 BOP surplus at $4.0 bln.

text.p: The Philippines Central Bank said on Thursday it is expecting a balance of payments surplus of about $4.0 billion by the end of the year, up from $631 million in 1995.
A year-end report issued by the bank also said the current account deficit would rise to 4.2 percent of gross national product this year, wider than the 2.6 percent in 1995.

"As a result of sustained investor confidence, large amounts of private capital inflows, in the form of foreign investments and loans, continued to flow into the economy to more than adequately finance the current account deficit," the report said.
The widening current account deficit should not worry investors since it is still one of the lowest in the region, the report said.
Current account deficits in Malaysia, Thailand and Indonesia are currently projected at 8.2 percent, 7.9 percent, and 3.6 percent of their gross domestic products respectively, it added.
The bank also projected the Philippines' gross international reserves to reach $11.5 billion by the end of the year, 47 percent higher than at end-1995.
Merchandise exports are expected to reach $20.5 billion this year, a 17.0 percent growth from last year, which is said to be in line with the government's target.

"The improving external position is also reflected in the steady decline in external debt indicators. The external debt service ratio, has fallen to about 12 percent in 1996 (January-August) compared with 15 percent in 1995 and 27 percent in 1991," the report added.
